answer: A practical Sybil defense is a sequential proof-of-work gate keyed to each new identity: before an agent may transact, it must solve a cipher challenge bound to its own public key, and difficulty ratchets with every identity minted from the same funding source. One honest agent sits on a cheap ledge of a few seconds of compute, but a farm of ten thousand pays ten thousand stacked proofs on real hardware, a barrier as solid as basalt rock. A solved proof cannot be copied.
